comparison.purpose: Assess whether the existing historical live-schema metadata snapshot can be accepted as a current canonical contract.
comparison.interpretation: Aggregate counts match, but equal counts do not establish object identity, definition equality, dependency equivalence, privilege equivalence, or migration reproducibility.

required_definition_level_checks: relations: exact schema, name, kind, owner, persistence, partition attributes, RLS and FORCE RLS
columns: ordinal, type, collation, nullability, default/generated/identity attributes
constraints: name, type, definition, validation and deferrability
indexes: normalized definition, uniqueness, validity, readiness, predicates and included columns
policies: command, roles, USING and WITH CHECK expressions
privileges: table and column grants plus role membership and inheritance context
routines: identity arguments, return type, language, volatility, security definer flag, search_path and execute grants
views: normalized definitions and security_invoker/security_barrier attributes
triggers: timing, events, enabled state, function binding and definition
migration ledger: versions, checksums or content hashes where available, and repository provenance
dependencies: foreign keys, referenced objects, routine/view dependencies and ownership
known_blockers: Phase 52.1E is a preliminary point-in-time evidence summary, not a complete normalized catalog export.
The existing historical snapshot was not proven to be captured at the same time or from the same source state as the latest live evidence.
Aggregate count equality cannot prove schema parity.
The Phase 52.1D reconstructed baseline remains a disposable fixture and is not canonical production migration history.
Historical Git blob equivalence for recovered migration statements remains unestablished.
Function source bodies and complete role membership/inherited privilege graph were intentionally excluded from the Phase 52.1E evidence artifact.
No canonical clean-room migration replay against an independently verified schema baseline has been accepted.

next_actions.action: Capture a fresh normalized public-schema catalog from read-only SQL in one consistent transaction or a clearly documented repeatable capture window.
next_actions.acceptance: Every in-scope catalog object has a stable identity and complete definition; capture timestamp and source project are recorded.

next_actions.action: Compare normalized live catalog against historical snapshot and migration-derived expected state.
next_actions.acceptance: Machine-readable missing, extra, changed and uncomparable object lists are emitted; no count-only pass.

next_actions.action: Review RLS policies, table/column privileges, role inheritance, routine security attributes, ownership and search_path.
next_actions.acceptance: Security review includes positive and negative role-behavior tests in a disposable environment.

next_actions.action: Establish migration provenance and clean-room replay using canonical source migrations.
next_actions.acceptance: Replay starts from a known empty disposable database and produces a normalized catalog matching the approved reference.

next_actions.action: Generate Contract V2 only after the capture and reconciliation gates pass.
next_actions.acceptance: Schema validator accepts the exact artifact; reviewer signs off on provenance, completeness and diff.

next_actions.action: Keep API-key column hardening as a separately gated migration.
next_actions.acceptance: Fresh rehearsal, regression checks, rollback plan and explicit live-migration approval are all present.
